concepts.title: Gerundio: cause, time, manner; gerundio passato
concepts.rule: The gerundio (parlando, essendo) replaces a clause of time, cause, manner or condition; the gerundio passato (avendo finito, essendo arrivata) marks an earlier action. Its implicit subject must be the subject of the main clause. After prepositions, English -ing becomes an Italian infinitive, not a gerund.
assessment: Forms the gerundio and gerundio passato, including fare → facendo, dire → dicendo
Uses the gerund for time, cause, manner and condition, and pur + gerund for concession
Keeps the same subject in the gerund and the main clause (avoids the dangling gerund)
Uses an infinitive, not a gerund, after prepositions and as a subject (prima di partire, nuotare fa bene)
Attaches pronouns to the gerund (vedendolo, avendogli parlato)

lesson.intro: Italian loves the gerund as a compact way to say 'while, because, by, if': *Tornando a casa, ho incontrato Paolo*. But it's a false friend for English speakers: English *-ing* is everywhere (*before leaving, I like swimming*), while the Italian gerund is never used after a preposition or as a noun. And its subject must match the main clause, or the sentence says something you didn't mean.

rules.title: Form
rules.text: -are → **-ando** (parlando); -ere/-ire → **-endo** (prendendo, partendo). Irregular stems come from the old Latin infinitive: *fare → facendo, dire → dicendo, bere → bevendo, porre → ponendo, tradurre → traducendo*. Gerundio passato: **avendo / essendo** + participle (*avendo finito, essendo arrivata*); with *essendo* the participle agrees.

examples.it: **Facendo** sport ogni giorno, si sente meglio.
examples.en: By doing sport every day, he feels better.

examples.it: **Avendo perso** l'ultimo autobus, abbiamo preso un taxi.
examples.en: Having missed the last bus, we took a taxi.

rules.title: What it can mean
rules.text: Time (= *mentre, quando*), cause (= *siccome, poiché*), manner or means (= *by…*), condition (= *se*), and with **pur** concession (= *anche se*). Context tells you which.

rules.title: Same subject!
rules.text: The gerund's implicit subject is the subject of the main clause. *Uscendo di casa, ho visto Marta* = **I** was leaving. If the subjects differ, use an explicit clause: *Mentre Marta usciva di casa, l'ho vista*. A sentence like ~~Aspettando l'autobus, un ladro mi ha rubato il portafoglio~~ literally says the **thief** was waiting for the bus. (Formal Italian can give the gerund its own subject, placed after it: *Essendo Marco malato, la riunione è stata rinviata*.)

examples.it: Mentre aspettavo l'autobus, un ladro mi ha rubato il portafoglio.
examples.en: While I was waiting for the bus, a thief stole my wallet.

rules.title: English -ing ≠ gerundio
rules.text: After a preposition, and when the verb is a subject or object, Italian uses the **infinitive**: *prima di partire* (before leaving), *senza dire niente* (without saying anything), *Mi piace nuotare* (I like swimming), *Fumare fa male* (Smoking is bad for you). Only English 'by -ing' becomes a bare gerund: *by studying = studiando*.

examples.it: Prima di **partire**, chiudi le finestre.
examples.en: Before leaving, close the windows.

examples.it: **Studiando** ogni giorno, supererai l'esame.
examples.en: By studying every day, you'll pass the exam.

rules.title: Pronouns attach
rules.text: Unstressed pronouns are attached to the end of the gerund (to *avendo/essendo* in the past form): *vedendolo, dicendoglielo, avendogli parlato, essendosi alzata*.

examples.it: **Vedendolo** così triste, ho deciso di aiutarlo.
examples.en: Seeing him so sad, I decided to help him.

mistakes.wrong: Prima di partendo, chiudi le finestre.
mistakes.right: Prima di partire, chiudi le finestre.
mistakes.why: After a preposition Italian uses the infinitive, never the gerund.
English 'swimming' here is a noun-like -ing: Italian uses the infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Essendo arrivato tardi, il professore mi ha rimproverato.
mistakes.right: Siccome ero arrivato tardi, il professore mi ha rimproverato.
mistakes.why: The gerund's subject is the main subject: as written, it's the professor who arrived late.
The gerundio passato keeps the verb's auxiliary: *uscire* → *essendo uscito*.
Pronouns attach to the end of the gerund.

tips: Translate 'by -ing' with a bare gerund, but 'before/after/without -ing' with *prima di / dopo / senza* + infinitive.
Check the subject: who is doing the gerund action? If it's not the main subject, rewrite with *mentre / siccome*.
*Pur* + gerund is a neat C1 way to say 'although': *Pur sapendolo, non ha detto niente*.

exercises.prompt: Ho imparato l'italiano ___ (guardare) film in lingua originale.

traps.why: 'By watching' (means) is a bare gerund in Italian: *guardando*.
-are verbs take *-ando*: *guardando*.

exercises.en: I learned Italian by watching films in the original language.

exercises.prompt: ___ (fare) attenzione, eviterai molti errori.

traps.why: *Fare* builds its gerund on the old stem *fac-*: *facendo*.

exercises.en: By paying attention, you'll avoid lots of mistakes.

exercises.prompt: ___ (essere) stanca, Laura è andata a letto presto.

traps.why: That's Spanish! Italian: *essendo*.

exercises.explanation: Cause → gerund: *essendo stanca* = siccome era stanca.
exercises.en: Being tired, Laura went to bed early.

exercises.prompt: ___ (perdere) l'ultimo autobus, abbiamo dovuto prendere un taxi.

traps.why: Missing the bus happened before taking the taxi: gerundio passato *avendo perso*.
*Perdere* takes *avere*: *avendo perso*.

exercises.en: Having missed the last bus, we had to take a taxi.

exercises.prompt: ___ (arrivare) in ritardo, le ragazze non hanno trovato posto.

traps.why: With *essendo* the participle agrees with *le ragazze*: *arrivate*.
*Arrivare* takes *essere*: *essendo arrivate*.
Also possible; *essendo arrivate* stresses that the late arrival came first and caused the problem.

exercises.en: Having arrived late, the girls didn't find a seat.

exercises.prompt: Before leaving, close the windows.
options: Prima di partendo, chiudi le finestre.
Prima di partire, chiudi le finestre.
Prima partendo, chiudi le finestre.

optionWhy.0: After a preposition (*prima di*), Italian uses the infinitive, not the gerund.

exercises.en: Before leaving, close the windows.

exercises.instruction: Which sentences are correct in careful Italian? (More than one may be.)
exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence(s).
options: Uscendo di casa, ha cominciato a piovere.
Uscendo di casa, ho visto che pioveva.
Mentre uscivo di casa, ha cominciato a piovere.

optionWhy.0: Dangling gerund: the main subject is the rain, so it literally says the rain was leaving the house. Use *Mentre uscivo…*

exercises.explanation: The gerund takes the main clause's subject. Different subjects → explicit clause with *mentre*.
exercises.en: As I was leaving the house, it started raining / I saw it was raining.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite with a gerund instead of the 'siccome' clause.
exercises.prompt: Siccome non sapevo la strada, ho chiesto a un passante.
answers: Non sapendo la strada, ho chiesto a un passante

traps.why: Replace the whole *siccome* clause with a gerund: *Non sapendo…*
*Sapere* → *sapendo*.

exercises.en: Not knowing the way, I asked a passer-by.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite with a gerund instead of the 'mentre' clause.
exercises.prompt: Mentre tornavo a casa, ho incontrato Paolo.
answers: Tornando a casa, ho incontrato Paolo
Ho incontrato Paolo tornando a casa

traps.why: The gerund replaces *mentre* + verb entirely: *Tornando a casa…*

exercises.en: On my way home, I ran into Paolo.

exercises.prompt: Dato che aveva già visto il film, Marco è rimasto a casa.
answers: Avendo già visto il film, Marco è rimasto a casa
Marco, avendo già visto il film, è rimasto a casa

traps.why: He saw the film earlier: gerundio passato *avendo visto*.
*Vedere* takes *avere*: *avendo visto*.

exercises.en: Having already seen the film, Marco stayed at home.

exercises.instruction: This sentence has a dangling gerund (it says the thief was waiting). Rewrite it with 'mentre' + imperfetto.
exercises.prompt: Aspettando l'autobus, un ladro mi ha rubato il portafoglio.
answers: Mentre aspettavo l'autobus, un ladro mi ha rubato il portafoglio
Un ladro mi ha rubato il portafoglio mentre aspettavo l'autobus

traps.why: Keep no gerund here: the subjects differ (I was waiting, the thief stole).
*I* was waiting: *aspettavo*.
Waiting was in progress: imperfetto *aspettavo*.

exercises.en: While I was waiting for the bus, a thief stole my wallet.

exercises.prompt: I like swimming.

traps.why: English uses -ing as a noun here; Italian uses the infinitive: *Mi piace nuotare*.
*Mi piace il nuoto* (the noun) is also fine. With a verb: *Mi piace nuotare*.

exercises.en: I like swimming.

exercises.prompt: By studying every day, you'll pass the exam.

traps.why: *Per studiare* = in order to study. 'By -ing' is a bare gerund: *studiando*.
No preposition: 'by -ing' = bare gerund *studiando*.

exercises.en: By studying every day, you'll pass the exam.

exercises.prompt: Although he is rich, he lives modestly.
answers: Pur essendo ricco, vive (modestamente|in modo modesto|semplicemente|in modo semplice)

traps.why: The task asks for the implicit form: *pur* + gerund (*Pur essendo ricco*).
Use the gerund in the first part: *Pur essendo ricco*.

exercises.en: Although he is rich, he lives modestly.

exercises.prompt: Seeing him so sad, I decided to help him.
answers: Vedendolo così triste, ho deciso di aiutarlo
Ho deciso di aiutarlo vedendolo così triste
exercises.explanation: The pronoun attaches to the gerund (*vedendolo*) and to the infinitive (*aiutarlo*).

exercises.prompt: Non ___ (conoscere + lo) bene, preferisco non giudicarlo.

traps.why: Unstressed pronouns attach to the end of the gerund: *conoscendolo*.

exercises.en: Not knowing him well, I'd rather not judge him.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian with a gerund.
exercises.prompt: Explain that you learned to cook by watching your grandmother.
answers: Ho imparato a cucinare guardando (mia nonna|la nonna)

traps.why: 'By watching' is a bare gerund: *guardando*.
Here the gerund expresses the means: *guardando*.

traps.match: Ho imparato cucinare guardando (mia nonna|la nonna)
traps.why: *Imparare a* + infinitive: *ho imparato a cucinare*.

exercises.en: I learned to cook by watching my grandmother.

concepts.title: Absolute participle (Finito il lavoro, …)
concepts.rule: The participio assoluto (Finito il lavoro, …; Arrivati a casa, …) replaces a time or cause clause for an action completed before the main one. With transitive verbs it agrees with the object; with essere verbs it agrees with the subject.
assessment: Uses the absolute participle for an earlier action (Finita la cena, …)
Makes the participle agree with the object (transitive verbs) or the subject (essere verbs)
Avoids it with intransitive verbs that take avere (dormire, camminare)
Recognises fixed phrases: detto questo, fatto sta, considerato che, una volta finito…
Attaches pronouns in formal style (Salutatili, Alzatasi)

lesson.intro: The absolute participle is a hallmark of good written Italian and of news reports: *Finita la riunione, il ministro ha parlato ai giornalisti*. English needs 'once / after + clause'; Italian just uses the participle. The tricky part for English speakers is **agreement**: the participle agrees with the noun it refers to, which usually comes right after it.

rules.title: What it does
rules.text: It replaces a clause with *dopo che, quando, appena, siccome* for an action **completed before** the main one. It's formal-neutral, very common in writing and news, and in set phrases in speech.

examples.it: **Finito** il lavoro, siamo andati a cena.
examples.en: Once the work was done, we went to dinner.

examples.it: **Detto** questo, sono d'accordo con te.
examples.en: Having said that, I agree with you.

rules.title: Transitive verbs: agree with the object
rules.text: The noun after the participle is its object, and the participle agrees with it in gender and number.

rules.title: Essere verbs: agree with the subject
rules.text: With verbs like *arrivare, partire, uscire, entrare*, the participle agrees with its subject. Normally that's the main subject (*Arrivata a casa, Anna…*). If it has a different subject, that subject must be stated after it: *Partiti gli ospiti, la casa tornò silenziosa.*

examples.it: **Arrivati** a casa, i ragazzi hanno cenato.
examples.en: Once they got home, the boys had dinner.

examples.it: **Partiti** gli ospiti, la casa è tornata silenziosa.
examples.en: Once the guests had left, the house went quiet again.

rules.title: Limits and pronouns
rules.text: Not possible with intransitive verbs that take *avere* (*dormire, camminare, viaggiare*): use *dopo aver dormito*. Pronouns attach to the participle in formal style: *Salutatili, se ne andò; Alzatasi, aprì la finestra*. *Una volta* or *appena* can come first: *Una volta finito il corso, …*

examples.it: **Dopo aver dormito** bene, si è alzato di buon umore. (not ~~Dormito bene~~)
examples.en: Having slept well, he got up in a good mood.

mistakes.why: The participle agrees with its object *la cena*.

mistakes.wrong: Arrivato a casa, Maria ha cenato.
mistakes.right: Arrivata a casa, Maria ha cenato.
mistakes.why: *Arrivare* takes *essere*: the participle agrees with Maria.

mistakes.right: Dopo aver dormito bene, mi sono alzato.
mistakes.why: Intransitive verbs with *avere* can't form an absolute participle.

mistakes.wrong: Arrivati alla stazione, il treno era partito.
mistakes.right: Arrivati alla stazione, abbiamo visto che il treno era partito.
mistakes.why: The participle refers to the main subject: as written, the train arrived at the station.

tips: Look right: the noun just after the participle decides the ending (*Chiuse le porte*).
Learn the fixed phrases: *detto questo / ciò detto, fatto sta che, considerato che, dato che, visto che*.

exercises.prompt: ___ (finire) la cena, siamo andati a fare una passeggiata.

traps.why: The participle agrees with its object *la cena* (feminine): *Finita*.
The walk came after dinner was over: participle *Finita*, not gerund.

exercises.explanation: Transitive verb → agrees with the object: **Finita** la cena.
exercises.en: Once dinner was over, we went for a walk.

exercises.prompt: ___ (arrivare) a casa, Anna ha acceso il riscaldamento.

traps.why: *Arrivare* takes *essere*: the participle agrees with Anna: *Arrivata*.

exercises.en: Once she got home, Anna switched on the heating.

exercises.prompt: ___ (chiudere) le finestre, siamo usciti.

traps.why: Agree with the object *le finestre* (feminine plural): *Chiuse*.

exercises.en: Having closed the windows, we went out.

exercises.prompt: ___ (leggere) i documenti, il giudice ha preso una decisione.

traps.why: Agree with *i documenti* (masculine plural): *Letti*.
The participle of *leggere* is *letto*.

exercises.en: Having read the documents, the judge made a decision.

exercises.prompt: ___ (partire) gli ospiti, la casa è tornata silenziosa.

traps.why: The participle has its own subject, *gli ospiti* (masculine plural): *Partiti*.

exercises.explanation: Different subject, stated after the participle: **Partiti** gli ospiti.
exercises.en: Once the guests had left, the house went quiet again.

exercises.prompt: Dopo che abbiamo pagato il conto, siamo usciti.
answers: [Una volta] pagato il conto, siamo usciti

traps.why: The absolute participle drops *dopo che* and the auxiliary: *Pagato il conto, …*
*Il conto* is masculine singular: *pagato*.

exercises.en: Having paid the bill, we left.

exercises.prompt: Dopo che fu entrata in casa, la ragazza si tolse il cappotto.
answers: [Una volta] entrata in casa, la ragazza si tolse il cappotto

traps.why: *Entrare* takes *essere*: agree with *la ragazza*: *Entrata*.
Drop *dopo che* and the auxiliary: *Entrata in casa, …*

exercises.en: Once she was inside, the girl took off her coat.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite with an absolute participle (formal style).
exercises.prompt: Appena si sono svegliati, i bambini hanno chiesto la colazione.
answers: (Svegliatisi|Appena svegliati|Appena svegli|Una volta svegli), i bambini hanno chiesto la colazione

traps.why: Drop the auxiliary: *Svegliatisi, …* or *Appena svegli, …*
Agree with *i bambini*: *svegliatisi / svegliati*.
In the absolute participle the pronoun attaches: *Svegliatisi*.

exercises.explanation: Reflexive verbs attach the pronoun: **Svegliatisi** (formal), or simply *Appena svegli*.
exercises.en: As soon as they woke up, the children asked for breakfast.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Finito il compito, Marco è uscito.
Finita il compito, Marco è uscito.
Finito i compiti, Marco è uscito.
exercises.explanation: Agree with the object: *Finito il compito / Finiti i compiti*.
exercises.en: Once he'd finished his homework, Marco went out.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Arrivati alla stazione, il treno era già partito.
Arrivati alla stazione, abbiamo scoperto che il treno era già partito.

optionWhy.0: The participle refers to the main subject, *il treno*: it says the train arrived at the station. The subjects must match.

exercises.explanation: Same subject (noi) in the participle and the main clause.
exercises.en: When we got to the station, we found the train had already left.

exercises.prompt: Find the incorrect sentence.
options: Dormito bene, si è alzato di buon umore.
Dopo aver dormito bene, si è alzato di buon umore.
Fatta colazione, si è alzato da tavola.

optionWhy.1: Correct: dopo + past infinitive works with any verb.
optionWhy.2: Correct: *fare colazione* is transitive, so *Fatta colazione* is fine.

exercises.explanation: *Dormire* is intransitive with *avere*: no absolute participle. Use *Dopo aver dormito*.
exercises.en: Spot the impossible absolute participle.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian with an absolute participle.
exercises.prompt: Once the decision was made, nobody talked about it any more.
answers: [Una volta] presa la decisione, nessuno ne ha più parlato
[Una volta] presa la decisione, nessuno ne parlò più
[Una volta] presa la decisione, non ne ha più parlato nessuno

traps.why: *La decisione* is feminine: *presa*.
In Italian you *prendere* a decision: *presa la decisione*.
The absolute participle needs no *dopo*: *Presa la decisione, …*

exercises.en: Once the decision was made, nobody talked about it any more.

exercises.prompt: Having said that, I agree with you.
answers: (Detto questo|Detto ciò|Ciò detto), sono d'accordo con te

traps.match: Avendo detto (questo|ciò)[,] sono d'accordo con te
traps.why: Grammatical, but it's a calque. The fixed phrase is *Detto questo*.
The idiom is the participle: *Detto questo*.

exercises.explanation: Fixed absolute participle: *Detto questo / Detto ciò*.
exercises.en: Having said that, I agree with you.

exercises.prompt: Once the exams were over, we left for Greece.
answers: Finiti gli esami, siamo partiti per la Grecia
Siamo partiti per la Grecia finiti gli esami
exercises.explanation: The absolute participle usually comes first, followed by its noun: *Finiti gli esami, …*

exercises.instruction: Complete with the absolute participle + pronoun (formal style).
exercises.prompt: Gli amici erano venuti a salutarla. ___ (salutare + li) in fretta, Marta salì sul treno.

traps.why: In the absolute participle the pronoun attaches to the end: *Salutatili*.
The participle agrees with the object *li* (the friends, masculine plural): *Salutatili*.

exercises.en: Her friends had come to say goodbye. Having said a quick goodbye to them, Marta got on the train.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian, starting with an absolute participle.
exercises.prompt: Once dinner was over, we watched a film.
answers: [Una volta] finita la cena, abbiamo (guardato|visto) un film

traps.why: *La cena* is feminine: *finita*.
Start with the participle: *Finita la cena, …*

exercises.en: Once dinner was over, we watched a film.

concepts.title: Past infinitive and the nominalised infinitive
concepts.rule: The past infinitive (aver(e) mangiato, essere uscita) marks an earlier action after dopo, per (cause), senza and verbs + di; with essere the participle agrees. The infinitive can also act as a masculine noun: (il) viaggiare, il suo continuo lamentarsi.
assessment: Uses dopo + past infinitive, never dopo + simple infinitive
Chooses avere/essere and makes the participle agree (dopo essere uscita)
Uses the past infinitive after di and per for earlier actions and causes (per aver superato)
Attaches pronouns to the auxiliary and agrees with lo/la (dopo averla vista)
Uses the infinitive as a noun subject, with article and modifiers (il suo continuo lamentarsi)

lesson.intro: Where English says 'after eating', 'sorry for being late' or 'fined for speeding', Italian uses the **past infinitive**: *dopo aver mangiato, scusa per essere arrivato in ritardo, multato per aver superato il limite*. And where English uses an -ing noun ('Travelling broadens the mind'), Italian uses the infinitive as a noun: *Viaggiare apre la mente*.

rules.title: Form
rules.text: **avere / essere** + past participle. *Avere* is often shortened to *aver* (*aver mangiato*). With *essere* the participle agrees with the subject (*dopo essere uscita / usciti*).

rules.title: dopo + past infinitive
rules.text: *Dopo* + infinitive always uses the **past** infinitive, with the same subject as the main clause.

examples.it: **Dopo aver mangiato**, siamo usciti.
examples.en: After eating, we went out.

examples.it: **Dopo essere uscita** dall'ufficio, Giulia è andata in palestra.
examples.en: After leaving the office, Giulia went to the gym.

rules.title: Other uses: di, per, senza
rules.text: Verb + *di* for earlier actions (*Penso di aver capito, Mi dispiace di averti disturbato*). **Per** + past infinitive = cause, 'for having done': *È stato multato per aver superato il limite* (*per* + simple infinitive = purpose). *Senza aver(e)…* = without having…

examples.it: Mi dispiace di **non essere venuto** alla tua festa.
examples.en: I'm sorry I didn't come to your party.

examples.it: È stato multato **per aver superato** il limite di velocità.
examples.en: He was fined for speeding.

rules.title: Pronouns
rules.text: Pronouns attach to the auxiliary: *dopo averlo visto, dopo esserci andati, dopo essersi alzata*. With *lo, la, li, le* the participle agrees: *dopo averla vista*.

examples.it: Ho visitato la mostra: **dopo averla vista**, ho capito perché tutti ne parlavano.
examples.en: I visited the exhibition: after seeing it, I understood why everyone talked about it.

rules.title: The nominalised infinitive
rules.text: Any infinitive can work as a masculine noun: as a subject often without an article (*Viaggiare apre la mente*), or with an article, adjectives and possessives (*il mangiare sano, il suo continuo lamentarsi, lo scorrere del tempo*). Use *lo* before s + consonant. English '-ing' as a noun = Italian infinitive, never the gerund.

examples.it: **Il suo continuo lamentarsi** mi irrita.
examples.en: His constant complaining annoys me.

examples.it: Mi spaventa **lo scorrere** del tempo.
examples.en: The passing of time frightens me.

mistakes.why: *Dopo* takes the past infinitive. (*Dopo mangiato* is heard in speech, but it's not standard.)
With *essere* the participle agrees with the subject.
A direct object pronoun *la* before the participle forces agreement.
An activity used as a subject is an infinitive, not a gerund.

tips: *Per* + simple infinitive = in order to; *per* + past infinitive = because of having done.
*Il dolce far niente*: the nominalised infinitive is also in many set phrases.

exercises.prompt: Dopo ___ (mangiare), siamo usciti a fare una passeggiata.

traps.why: *Dopo* + infinitive needs the past infinitive: *dopo aver mangiato*.
*Dopo mangiato* is heard in casual speech, but standard Italian says *dopo aver mangiato*.
*Mangiare* takes *avere*.

exercises.en: After eating, we went out for a walk.

exercises.prompt: Dopo ___ (uscire) dall'ufficio, Giulia è andata in palestra.

traps.why: *Uscire* takes *essere*: *dopo essere uscita*.
With *essere* the participle agrees with Giulia: *uscita*.
*Dopo* needs the past infinitive: *dopo essere uscita*.

exercises.en: After leaving the office, Giulia went to the gym.

exercises.prompt: Dopo ___ (arrivare) a Roma, i miei amici hanno cercato un albergo.

traps.why: Agree with *i miei amici*: *arrivati*.
*Arrivare* takes *essere*.

exercises.en: After arriving in Rome, my friends looked for a hotel.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the past infinitive. The speaker is a man.
exercises.prompt: Mi dispiace di non ___ (venire) alla tua festa sabato scorso.

traps.why: The party was last Saturday: use the past infinitive, *essere venuto*.
*Venire* takes *essere*.
The speaker is a man: *venuto*.

exercises.explanation: Earlier action after *dispiacere di* → past infinitive.
exercises.en: I'm sorry I didn't come to your party last Saturday.

exercises.prompt: È stato multato per ___ (superare) il limite di velocità.

traps.why: *Per* + simple infinitive means 'in order to'. For the cause ('for speeding'), use *per aver superato*.
No gerund after a preposition: *per aver superato*.

exercises.en: He was fined for exceeding the speed limit.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the past infinitive + pronoun (la = la mostra).
exercises.prompt: Ho visitato la mostra: dopo ___ (vedere + la), ho capito perché tutti ne parlavano.

traps.why: With *la* before the participle, it must agree: *averla vista*.
The pronoun attaches to the auxiliary: *averla vista*.

exercises.explanation: Pronoun on the auxiliary + agreement: **averla vista**.
exercises.en: I visited the exhibition: after seeing it, I understood why everyone was talking about it.

exercises.prompt: Dopo ___ (alzarsi), Chiara ha fatto la doccia.

traps.why: Agree with Chiara: *alzata*.
Reflexive verbs take *essere*: *essersi alzata*.
The reflexive pronoun attaches to the auxiliary: *essersi*.

exercises.en: After getting up, Chiara had a shower.

exercises.prompt: ___ troppo zucchero fa male alla salute.
options: Mangiare
Mangiando
Il mangiando
Mangiato

optionWhy.1: A gerund can't be the subject of a sentence: use the infinitive.
optionWhy.2: The gerund can't take an article.
optionWhy.3: The participle doesn't work as a subject here.

exercises.explanation: English '-ing' as subject = Italian infinitive: *Mangiare troppo zucchero…*
exercises.en: Eating too much sugar is bad for your health.

exercises.prompt: Mi dà fastidio il suo continuo ___.
options: lamentarsi
lamentandosi
lamentare
lamentato

optionWhy.1: A gerund can't act as a noun with *il suo continuo*.
optionWhy.2: *Lamentare* (non-reflexive) means to report or deplore something (*lamentare un danno*). 'Complaining' is *lamentarsi*.
optionWhy.3: A participle doesn't fit after *il suo continuo*.

exercises.explanation: Nominalised infinitive with article, possessive and adjective: *il suo continuo lamentarsi*.
exercises.en: His constant complaining annoys me.

exercises.prompt: Mi spaventa ___ scorrere del tempo.

traps.why: Nominalised infinitives are masculine and follow the normal rules: *lo* before s + consonant (*lo scorrere*).
Nominalised infinitives are masculine: *lo scorrere*.

exercises.en: The passing of time frightens me.

exercises.instruction: Combine into one sentence with dopo + past infinitive. The speaker is a man.
exercises.prompt: Ho finito i compiti, poi sono uscito.
answers: Dopo aver[e] finito i compiti, sono uscito
Sono uscito dopo aver[e] finito i compiti

traps.why: *Dopo* needs the past infinitive: *dopo aver finito*.
*Finire i compiti* takes *avere*.

exercises.en: After finishing my homework, I went out.

exercises.instruction: Combine into one sentence with dopo + past infinitive, replacing 'la lettera' with a pronoun in the first part. The speaker is a man.
exercises.prompt: Ho letto la lettera, poi l'ho strappata.

traps.why: With *la* attached, the participle agrees: *averla letta*.
*Dopo* needs the past infinitive: *dopo averla letta*.

exercises.explanation: Pronoun on the auxiliary + agreement: *averla letta*.
exercises.en: After reading it, I tore it up.

exercises.prompt: After leaving the house, she realised she had forgotten her phone.
answers: Dopo (essere|esser) uscita (di|da) casa, si è (accorta|resa conto) (di aver[e] dimenticato|che aveva dimenticato) il [suo] (telefono|cellulare)

traps.why: The subject is *lei*: *dopo essere uscita*.
'After -ing' = *dopo* + past infinitive: *dopo essere uscita*.
'To realise' = *accorgersi, rendersi conto*.

exercises.explanation: *Dopo essere uscita* (agreement) + earlier action in the past infinitive or trapassato.
exercises.en: After leaving the house, she realised she had forgotten her phone.

exercises.prompt: Travelling broadens the mind.

traps.why: An activity as subject is an infinitive, not a gerund: *Viaggiare apre la mente*.

exercises.en: Travelling broadens the mind.

exercises.prompt: Thank you for helping me.
exercises.explanation: *Ringraziare per* + past infinitive: you thank someone for something already done. The pronoun attaches to *avere*.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian (informal), using a past infinitive.
exercises.prompt: Apologise to a friend for being late.

traps.why: *Arrivare* takes *essere*: *per essere arrivato/a*.
After *per / di* use the infinitive: *per essere arrivato/a*.
*Scusi* is formal. To a friend: *Scusa / Scusami*.

exercises.en: Sorry for being late.

concepts.title: Causative fare / lasciare + infinitive
concepts.rule: Fare + infinitive = to have something done or make someone do it (Faccio riparare la macchina); lasciare + infinitive = to let (Lascia parlare Marco). Pronouns go before fare (La faccio riparare), farsi + infinitive takes essere (Mi sono fatta tagliare i capelli), and lasciare che takes the subjunctive.
assessment: Uses fare + infinitive for having something done or making someone do something
Places object pronouns before fare (or attached to it), never on the infinitive
Marks the person with a / da when there is also a thing (Faccio riparare la macchina al meccanico)
Uses farsi + infinitive with essere in compound tenses
Uses lasciare + infinitive and lasciare che + subjunctive

lesson.intro: English has several ways to say this: *have the car repaired, get your hair cut, make someone laugh, let someone speak*. Italian does it all with **fare** or **lasciare** + infinitive. The traps for English speakers are word order (the infinitive goes straight after *fare*), pronoun position, and remembering that *Ho riparato la macchina* means you did it yourself.

rules.title: fare + infinitive
rules.text: To have something done, or to make someone do something. The infinitive comes **immediately after** *fare*; the thing or person follows.

examples.it: **Faccio riparare** la macchina.
examples.en: I'm having the car repaired.

examples.it: Il film mi **ha fatto piangere**.
examples.en: The film made me cry.

rules.title: Who does the action: a / da
rules.text: With only a person, it's a direct object (*La faccio ridere*). If there's also a thing, the person is introduced by **a** (or **da**, especially for services): *Faccio riparare la macchina al meccanico / dal meccanico*. As a pronoun, the person becomes indirect: *Gli ho fatto leggere la lettera*.

examples.it: Ho fatto controllare i freni **al** meccanico.
examples.en: I had the mechanic check the brakes.

examples.it: **Gli** ho fatto leggere la lettera.
examples.en: I made him read the letter.

rules.title: Pronouns go with fare
rules.text: Pronouns go before the conjugated *fare*, or attach to *fare* when it's an infinitive or an imperative: *La faccio riparare, Me la faccio riparare, Fammi sapere, Puoi farmela vedere?* In compound tenses *fare* takes *avere*, and the participle agrees with *lo/la/li/le*: *L'ho fatta riparare*.

head: Example
rows: Puoi far**mela** vedere? / **Me la** puoi far vedere?

rules.title: farsi + infinitive
rules.text: To have something done to or for yourself: *farsi tagliare i capelli, farsi accompagnare, farsi capire*. As a reflexive verb, it takes **essere** in compound tenses: *Mi sono fatta tagliare i capelli*.

examples.it: Giulia **si è fatta** accompagnare a casa.
examples.en: Giulia got someone to take her home.

rules.title: lasciare + infinitive / lasciare che + subjunctive
rules.text: *Lasciare* + infinitive = to let, allow (*Lascia parlare Marco, Lasciami stare*). *Lasciare che* + **subjunctive** is the explicit version: *Lascia che ti spieghi*, *Non lasciare che ti trattino così*.

examples.it: I miei non mi **lasciavano uscire** la sera.
examples.en: My parents wouldn't let me go out in the evening.

examples.it: **Lascia che** ti **spieghi**.
examples.en: Let me explain.

mistakes.wrong: Ho riparato la macchina dal meccanico.
mistakes.right: Ho fatto riparare la macchina dal meccanico.
mistakes.why: *Ho riparato* means you did the repair yourself. Getting it done is *fare riparare*.
In the causative, pronouns go with *fare*, not the infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Mi ho fatto tagliare i capelli.
mistakes.right: Mi sono fatto tagliare i capelli.

tips: 'Get/have something done' → *fare* + infinitive; 'get/have it done for yourself' → *farsi* + infinitive.
Don't calque 'let me know' as ~~lasciami sapere~~: Italians say *fammi sapere*.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence means that the mechanic did the repair?
exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence.
options: Ho riparato la macchina.
Ho fatto riparare la macchina.
Mi sono riparato la macchina.

optionWhy.0: *Ho riparato* means I repaired it myself.
optionWhy.2: This also suggests you did it yourself (for yourself).

exercises.en: I had the car repaired.

exercises.prompt: Il film era così triste che mi ha fatto ___ (piangere).

traps.why: *Fare* is followed directly by the infinitive, with no preposition.
Use the bare infinitive after *fare*: *mi ha fatto piangere*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare* + bare infinitive = to make someone do something.
exercises.en: The film was so sad it made me cry.

exercises.instruction: Complete with fare + mi in the right form.
exercises.prompt: Puoi ___ (fare + mi) sapere quando arrivi?

traps.why: With an infinitive, the pronoun attaches to the end: *farmi* (or *Mi puoi far sapere?*).
'Let me know' is *fammi / farmi sapere* in Italian, not *lasciare*.

exercises.en: Can you let me know when you arrive?

exercises.instruction: Complete with lasciare in the right tense.
exercises.prompt: Quando avevo quindici anni, i miei genitori non mi ___ (lasciare) uscire la sera.

traps.why: A general rule over a period of your life (*quando avevo quindici anni, la sera*) is a habit: imperfetto *lasciavano*.
*Fare uscire* = to make someone go out. 'To let' is *lasciare*.

exercises.en: When I was fifteen, my parents wouldn't let me go out in the evening.

exercises.prompt: Aspetta, non arrabbiarti: lascia che ti ___ (spiegare).

traps.why: *Lasciare che* takes the subjunctive: *(io) spieghi*.
Keep the hard *g* sound: *spieghi*.

exercises.en: Wait, don't get angry: let me explain.

exercises.prompt: Faccio riparare la bicicletta.

traps.why: In the causative, the pronoun goes before *fare*: *La faccio riparare*.
*La bicicletta* is feminine: *la*.

exercises.en: I'm having it repaired.

exercises.prompt: Ho fatto riparare la macchina.

traps.why: In careful Italian the participle agrees with the preceding *la*: *l'ho fatta riparare*.
The pronoun goes before the auxiliary: *L'ho fatta riparare*.

exercises.en: I had it repaired.

exercises.prompt: Mi faccio riparare la macchina.

traps.why: Before *lo/la/li/le/ne*, *mi* becomes *me*: *Me la faccio riparare*.
The indirect pronoun comes first: *me la*.
Pronouns go before *fare*: *Me la faccio riparare*.

exercises.en: I'm getting it repaired (for myself).

exercises.instruction: Complete with farsi in the passato prossimo.
exercises.prompt: Ieri Giulia ___ (farsi) tagliare i capelli cortissimi.

traps.why: *Farsi* is reflexive, so it takes *essere*: *si è fatta*.
With *essere* the participle agrees with Giulia: *fatta*.

exercises.en: Yesterday Giulia had her hair cut really short.

exercises.prompt: I had the mechanic check the brakes.
options: Ho fatto controllare i freni al meccanico.
Ho fatto il meccanico controllare i freni.
Ho fatto controllare il meccanico i freni.

optionWhy.2: With both a person and a thing, the person is introduced by *a* (or *da*): *al meccanico*.

exercises.en: I had the mechanic check the brakes.

exercises.prompt: Let me know!

traps.why: 'Let me know' is a fixed causative in Italian: *Fammi sapere*.
*Fa'* + *mi* doubles the consonant: *fammi*.
*Fatemi* addresses several people; to one friend: *Fammi sapere*.

exercises.en: Let me know!

exercises.prompt: Tomorrow I'm getting my hair cut.
answers: Domani (mi faccio|mi farò|vado a farmi) tagliare i capelli
(Mi faccio|Mi farò|Vado a farmi) tagliare i capelli domani

traps.why: *Mi taglio i capelli* means you cut them yourself. Getting it done: *mi faccio tagliare i capelli*.
Italian uses the reflexive, not a possessive, for your own body: *mi faccio tagliare i capelli*.

exercises.explanation: *Farsi* + infinitive = to get something done to yourself.
exercises.en: Tomorrow I'm getting my hair cut.

exercises.prompt: Don't let them treat you like that.
answers: Non lasciare che ti trattino (così|in quel modo|in questo modo)
Non (lasciarti|ti lasciare) trattare (così|in quel modo|in questo modo)

traps.why: *Lasciare che* takes the subjunctive: *che ti trattino*.
'Let' is *lasciare*, not *fare*.

exercises.en: Don't let them treat you like that.

exercises.prompt: I'm getting the mechanic to fix it for me.
answers: Me la faccio riparare dal meccanico
exercises.explanation: Combined pronoun before *faccio*, infinitive straight after, then *da* + the person.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the right preposition + article.
exercises.prompt: Il professore ha fatto ripetere l'esercizio ___ studenti.

traps.why: With both a thing (*l'esercizio*) and a person, the person takes *a* (or *da*): *agli studenti*.
Not *per*: the doer of a causative is marked with *a* or *da*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare* + inf + object + **a/da** + person (*agli* before s + consonant).
exercises.en: The teacher made the students repeat the exercise.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian, politely (Lei), with 'fare vedere'.
exercises.prompt: In a shop, ask the assistant if they can show you that bag.
answers: (Mi fa|Mi può far|Mi può fare|Può farmi|Potrebbe farmi|Mi potrebbe far|Mi potrebbe fare) vedere quella borsa[, per favore]

traps.why: In a shop, use *Lei*: *Mi fa vedere…? / Può farmi vedere…?*

traps.match: (Mi (può|potrebbe) mostrare|(Può|Potrebbe) mostrarmi) quella borsa[, per favore]
traps.why: *Mostrare* works too (*Mi può mostrare…?*), but *far vedere* is the everyday choice.

exercises.explanation: *Far vedere* = to show; pronoun before *fa* or attached to *fare*.
exercises.en: Could you show me that bag, please?

exercises.instruction: Choose the word that fits the meaning.
exercises.prompt: Mia madre mi ___ tornare tardi: si fidava di me.
options: lasciava
faceva
lasciava che

optionWhy.1: *Mi faceva tornare tardi* = she made me come home late. With *si fidava di me*, she allowed it: *lasciava*.
optionWhy.2: *Lasciare che* needs a subjunctive clause (*lasciava che tornassi tardi*), not an infinitive.

exercises.explanation: *Lasciare* + infinitive = to allow; *fare* + infinitive = to cause/oblige.
exercises.en: My mother let me come home late: she trusted me.
